title: Design a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Service
prompt: Design a retrieval-augmented generation service that answers user questions over a company's private documents (wikis, PDFs, tickets, code). It must ground answers in the corpus with citations, stay fresh as documents change, and control hallucination. Assume a large enterprise corpus and interactive latency.
blurb: The end-to-end RAG design — ingestion and chunking, embeddings, vector index, retrieval plus reranking, grounded generation, eval, and hallucination control.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (ingest, chunk, retrieve, ground, cite, refresh) from non-functional (answer latency, freshness SLA, grounding/faithfulness, access control per document).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about corpus size and modality mix, update rate, per-user document permissions, acceptable staleness, latency budget, and how quality will be measured.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Estimates chunk count, embedding dimension and vector index size (vectors x dim x 4 bytes plus graph overhead), embedding compute for backfill, query QPS, retrieval and LLM latency budget, token cost per answer.

rubric.label: Ingestion & chunking
rubric.description: Parsing heterogeneous sources, chunk sizing and overlap, semantic vs fixed chunking, metadata/ACL capture, dedup, and an idempotent incremental pipeline.

rubric.label: Retrieval & reranking
rubric.description: Embedding model choice, ANN vector search, hybrid lexical+dense (BM25) retrieval, metadata/ACL filtering, cross-encoder reranking, and top-k selection.

rubric.label: Grounding & generation
rubric.description: Prompt assembly with context window budgeting, citation enforcement, abstention when context is insufficient, and streaming the answer.

rubric.label: Freshness & embedding sync
rubric.description: Keeping the index in sync as source docs change — CDC on the source, re-embed only changed chunks, tombstone deletes, versioning; bounded staleness.

rubric.label: Evaluation & quality
rubric.description: Offline retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR/nDCG), end-to-end faithfulness/answer-relevance (LLM-as-judge + golden sets), and online feedback loops.

rubric.label: Hallucination control
rubric.description: Faithfulness grounding, citation/attribution checks, confidence thresholds, abstention, and guardrails against unsupported claims.

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Sharding the vector index, separating ingest/serve, caching embeddings and answers, autoscaling the LLM and reranker tiers.

rubric.label: ML system specifics
rubric.description: Embedding model versioning and reindex-on-model-change, hybrid retrieval tuning, reranker cost/latency tradeoff, and eval-driven iteration.

rubric.label: Security & access control
rubric.description: Per-document ACLs enforced at retrieval time, PII handling, prompt-injection defense from retrieved content, tenant isolation, and audit of sources used.

functional_requirements: Ingest heterogeneous private docs (wiki, PDF, tickets, code) into a searchable index
Answer natural-language questions grounded in retrieved chunks with citations
Retrieve, rerank, and assemble context within the model window
Refresh the index as source documents are added/edited/deleted
Abstain or say 'I don't know' when the corpus lacks an answer
Enforce per-user document permissions on what can be retrieved
nonfunctional_requirements: End-to-end answer latency budget ~2-5s p95 (streaming first token < 1s)
Freshness SLA: edited docs reflected within minutes
High retrieval recall so the answer's evidence is actually present
Faithfulness: answers grounded in and attributable to retrieved context
Multi-tenant isolation and no cross-tenant leakage
clarifying_questions: How large is the corpus (docs, total tokens) and what's the update rate?
Are there per-user/per-group document permissions we must enforce?
What staleness is acceptable after a doc changes?
What's the latency budget and expected query QPS?
How will we measure answer quality — golden set, human review, thumbs?
Self-hosted vs API LLM, and any data-residency constraints?
qualifying_questions: Is this single-turn Q&A or multi-turn conversational?
Do we need multimodal (tables, images) or text-only for v1?

estimations.traffic: ~50 QPS peak queries; each query = 1 embed + 1 ANN search + rerank of ~50 candidates + 1 LLM generation
estimations.corpus: 10M chunks (~5M docs x ~2 chunks avg after 500-token chunking)
estimations.index_size: 10M vectors x 768 dims x 4B ≈ 30GB raw; ~1.5-2x with HNSW graph ≈ 45-60GB — fits in RAM on a few nodes
estimations.embedding_backfill: 10M chunks / (few k chunks/s per GPU) ≈ hours on a small GPU pool; incremental is trivial
estimations.latency_budget: embed ~20ms + ANN ~10-30ms + rerank ~50-150ms + LLM ~1-3s; rerank and LLM dominate
estimations.token_cost: ~2-4k context tokens + ~500 output tokens per answer drives per-query LLM cost; cache repeated queries

core_components: Vector index / ANN store with metadata filtering
Context assembler / prompt builder with token budgeting
data_model: documents(doc_id PK, source, uri, owner, acl_groups, version, updated_at, checksum)
chunks(chunk_id PK, doc_id FK, ordinal, text, token_count, embed_model_version, vector_ref)
vectors(chunk_id, embedding[dim], acl_groups, metadata) — in ANN store
feedback(query_id, user_id, answer, cited_chunks[], rating, ts)
api_design: POST /ingest { source, uri | payload } → { doc_id, chunk_count, status }
POST /query { question, filters?, k? } → stream { tokens..., citations:[{chunk_id, doc_uri, score}] }
reference.high_level_design: Ingest path: source docs → parse → chunk (semantic, ~300-800 tokens, small overlap) → extract metadata + ACL → embed (batched on GPU) → upsert into vector index + BM25 index keyed by chunk_id. Query path: authenticate → embed query → hybrid retrieve (dense ANN + BM25) with ACL/metadata filter → merge/dedupe candidates → cross-encoder rerank top ~50 to top ~5-8 → assemble prompt within token budget → LLM generates a grounded, cited answer, streamed to the client. Feedback and citations are logged for eval. A sync worker watches source changes and re-embeds only changed chunks.

deep_dives.probe: Pure dense retrieval misses exact-match terms (IDs, error codes). How do you combine dense and lexical (BM25) — reciprocal rank fusion, weighted merge — and how do you tune it?
Your top-8 chunks don't fit the window, or none is relevant. How do you budget tokens, and how does the model decide to abstain instead of fabricating?
A doc is edited. Walk me through keeping the index consistent — do you re-embed the whole doc or only changed chunks, and how do you handle deletes and stale vectors?
How do you know retrieval quality and answer faithfulness didn't regress after you change the chunker or embedding model? What metrics and datasets?
The model cites a chunk but the claim isn't actually supported by it. How do you detect and prevent unsupported/mis-attributed statements?
You upgrade the embedding model. Old and new vectors aren't comparable — how do you reindex 10M chunks with zero downtime?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions vector database or vector index or embeddings
followup_bank.question: When a source document changes, how do the embeddings stay in sync — CDC on the source, re-embed only changed chunks, tombstone the old vectors? What's the staleness bound?
What do you cache — query embeddings, retrieved chunks, or full answers via a semantic cache? What's the eviction policy and how do you avoid serving a stale answer after the source doc changed?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or postgres or sql
followup_bank.question: How do you capture source-of-truth changes to drive re-embedding — CDC/Debezium vs polling vs dual writes?
Reranking is expensive per candidate. How many candidates do you rerank, and how do you bound its latency and cost?

scaling: Shard the vector index by tenant/namespace; replicate shards for read throughput
Separate ingest and serve tiers so backfills don't hurt query latency
Batch embedding requests on GPU; autoscale embed and rerank pools on queue depth
Cache query embeddings and (semantically) cache answers for repeated questions
Route short/simple queries to a smaller/cheaper LLM
bottlenecks: Reranker and LLM latency dominate the tail
Embedding backfill/reindex on model change is compute-heavy
ANN recall vs latency tradeoff under aggressive metadata filtering
Context window budget — too many chunks dilute grounding
tradeoffs: Larger chunks (more context, fewer boundaries) vs smaller chunks (sharper retrieval, more vectors)
Dense-only (semantic) vs hybrid (adds lexical exactness, more moving parts)
Rerank many candidates (better precision) vs latency/cost
Bigger LLM (better synthesis) vs smaller/cheaper with tighter grounding
Fresh index (frequent re-embed cost) vs bounded staleness
alternative_solutions: Long-context 'stuff the docs' without retrieval (only for tiny corpora)
Fine-tuning the LLM on the corpus instead of RAG (stale, costly, poor attribution)
GraphRAG / knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval for multi-hop questions
Agentic/iterative retrieval that reformulates queries across turns
observability: Retrieval recall@k and rerank score distributions (sampled/online)
Faithfulness/answer-relevance from LLM-judge on a rolling sample
First-token and end-to-end latency SLOs; abstention rate
Index freshness lag (source change → vector updated)
security: Enforce per-document ACLs at retrieval time (filter by user's groups) — never post-filter after generation
Treat retrieved content as untrusted — defend against prompt injection embedded in docs
Tenant isolation of indexes and caches
PII detection/redaction in ingest; audit which sources fed each answer
Rate-limit queries and ingestion per tenant
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer scopes the corpus, permissions, freshness, and how quality is measured; estimates chunk count, vector index size, and the latency budget (rerank + LLM dominate). It designs an idempotent ingest→chunk→embed→upsert pipeline capturing ACLs, and a query path of hybrid dense+lexical retrieval with ACL filtering, cross-encoder reranking, token-budgeted prompt assembly, and streamed cited generation with an explicit abstention path. It proactively addresses freshness (CDC re-embedding only changed chunks, tombstoning deletes, zero-downtime reindex on model change), evaluation (recall@k/nDCG offline, faithfulness via LLM-judge and golden sets, online feedback), and hallucination control (grounding, citation-support checks, confidence-based abstention). It names reranker/LLM latency and reindex compute as the main bottlenecks and enforces ACLs at retrieval time.

interviewer_notes: Let the candidate structure requirements before diving into vector search — many jump straight to 'embed and retrieve' and skip permissions, freshness, and eval. Push hard on three senior-signal areas: (1) freshness/embedding sync when source docs change — use the CDC/embedding-sync probe; (2) evaluation — if they can't describe retrieval and faithfulness metrics plus a golden set, that's a gap; (3) hallucination control and abstention. If they place a vector DB, probe filtering + ACL enforcement at retrieval time. If they mention a cache, probe semantic-cache eviction and staleness after doc edits. Weaker candidates treat RAG as a single LLM call; strong ones separate ingest/serve, reason about hybrid retrieval and reranking cost, and tie every design choice back to a measurable quality metric.
